passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
The longest bull run in a century of art-market history ended on a dramatic note with a sale of 56 works by Damien Hirst, Beautiful Inside My Head Forever, at Sotheby's in London on September 15th 2008.All but two pieces sold, fetching more than £70m, a record for a sale by a single artist. It was a last victory. As the auctioneer called out bids, in New York one of the oldest banks on Wall Street, Lehman Brothers, filed for bankruptcy.

The world art market had already been losing momentum for a while after rising bewilderingly since 2003. At its peak in 2007 it was worth some $65 billion, reckons Clare McAndrew, founder of Arts Economics, a research firm - double the figure five years earlier. Since then it may have come down to $50 billion. But the market generates interest far beyond its size because it brings together great wealth, few other industries.

In the weeks and months that followed Mr. Hirst's sale, spending of any sort became deeply unfashionable. In the art world that meant collectors stayed away from galleries and salerooms. Sales of contemporary art fell by two-thirds, and in the most overheated sector, they were down by nearly 90% in the year to November 2008. Within weeks the world's two biggest auction houses, Sotheby's and Christie's, had to pay out nearly $200m in guarantees to clients who had placedworksfor salewith them.

Thecurrentdownturnin the art market istheworstsincethe Japanese stopped buying Impressionists at the end of 1989. This time experts reckon that prices are about 40% down on their peak on average, though some have been far more fluctuant. But Edward Dolman, Christie's chief executive, says: “I'm pretty confident we're atthebottom."

What makes this slump different from the last, he says, is that there are still buyers in the market. Almost everyone who was interviewed for this special report said that the biggest problem at the moment is not a lack of demand but a lack ofgood work to sell. The threeDs-death, debtanddivorce-stilldeliverworksof arttothe market. But anyone who does not have to sell is keeping away, waiting for confidence to return.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
I was addressing a small gathering in a suburban Virginia living room - a women's group that had invited men to join them. Throughout the evening, one man had been particularly talkative, frequently offering ideas and anecdotes, while his wife sat silently beside him on the couch. Toward the end of the evening, I commented that women frequently complain that their husbands don't talk to them. This man quickly nodded in agreement. He gestured toward his wife and said, “She's the talker in our family." The room burst into laughter; come home from work I have nothing to say. If she didn't keep the conversation going, we'd spend the whole evening in silence."" This episode crystallizes the irony that although American men tend to talk more than women in public situations, they often talk less at home. And this pattern is wreaking havoc with marriage. The pattern was observed by political scientist Andrew Hacker in the late 1970s. Sociologist Catherine Kohler Riessman reports in her new book Divorce Talk that most of the women she interviewed -but only a few of the men-gave lack of communication as the reason for their divorces. Given the current divorce rate of nearly 50 percent, that amounts to millions of cases in the United States every year - a virtual epidemic offailed conversation.

In my own research, complaints from women about their husbands most often focused not on tangible inequities such as having doing far more than their share of daily life-support work like cleaning, cooking and social arrangements. Instead, they focused on found, as Hacker observed years before, that most wives want their husbands to be, first and foremost, conversational partners, but few husbandssharethis expectation of theirwives.

In short, the image that best represents the current crisis is the stereotypical cartoon scene of a man sitting at the breakfast table with a newspaper held up in front of his face, while a woman glares at the back of it, wanting to talk.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
Over the past decade, many companies had perfected the art of creating automatic behaviors - habits - among consumers. These habits have helped companies earn billions of dollars when customers eat snacks or wipe counters almost without thinking, often inresponse to a carefully designed set of daily cues. instead of a soap habit, that remain killers only because we can't figure out how to change people's habits,” said Dr. Curtis, the director of the Hygiene Center at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. “We wanted to learn from private industry how to create new behaviors that happen automatically."

The companies that Dr. Curtis turned to - Procter & Gamble, Colgate-Palmolive and Unilever - had invested hundreds of millions of dollars finding the subtle cues in consumers’ lives that corporations could use to introduce new routines.

If you look hard enough, you'll find that many of the products we use every day-chewing gums, skin moisturizers, disinfecting wipes, air fresheners, water purifiers, health snacks, teeth whiteners, fabric softeners, vitamins - are results of manufactured habits. A century ago, because of shrewd advertising and public health campaigns, many Americans habituallygive their pearly whites a cavity-preventing scrub twice a day, often with Colgate, Crest or one of the other brands. A few decades ago, many people didn't drink water outside of a meal. Then beverage companies started bottling the production of far-off springs, and now office workers unthinkingly sip bottled water all day long. Chewing gum, once bought primarily by adolescent boys, is nowfeaturedin commercials as abreathfreshener and teethcleanser for use after a meal. Skin moisturizers are advertised as part of morning beauty rituals, slipped in between hair brushing and putting onmakeup.

"Our products succeed when they become part of daily or weekly retired from Procter & Gamble, the company that sold $76 billion of Tide, Crest and other products last year. “Creating positive habits is a huge part of improving our consumers’ lives, and it's essential to making new products commercially viable."

Through experiments and observation, social scientists like Dr. Berning have learned that there is power in tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising.As this new science of habit has emerged, controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
Many Americans regard the jury system as a concrete expression of crucial democratic values, including the principles that all citizens who meet minimal qualifications of age and literacy are equally competent to serve on juries; that jurors should be selected randomly from a representative cross section of the community; that no citizen should be denied the right to serve on a jury on account of race, religion, sex, or national origin; that defendants are entitled to trial by their peers; and that verdicts should represent the conscience of the community and not just the letter of the law. The jury is also said to be the best surviving example of direct rather than representative democracy.In a direct democracy, citizens take turns governing themselves, rather than electing representatives to govern for them. But as recently as in 1968, jury selection procedures conflicted with these democratic ideals. In some states, for example, jury duty was limited to persons of supposedly superior intelligence, education, and moral character. Although the Supreme Court of the United States had prohibited intentional racial discrimination in jury selection as early as the 1880 case of Strauder v. West Virginia, the practice of selecting so-called elite or blue-ribbon juries provided a convenient way around this and other antidiscrimination laws.

The system also failed to regularly include women on juries until the mid-20th century. Although women first served on state juries in Utah in 1898, it was not until the 1940s that a majority of states made women eligible for jury duty. Even then several states automatically exempted women from jury duty unless they personally asked to have their names included on the jury list. This practice was justified by the claim that women were needed at home, and it kept juries unrepresentative of women through the 1960s.

In 1968,the Congress of the United States passed the Jury Selection and Service Act, ushering in a new era of democratic reforms for the jury. This law abolished special educational requirements for federal jurors and required them to be selected at random from a cross section of the entire community. In the landmark 1975 decision Taylor v. Louisiana, the Supreme Court extended the requirement that juries be representative of all parts of the community to the statelevel. TheTaylordecision alsodeclared sex discrimination in jury selection to be unconstitutional and ordered states to use the sameproceduresfor selectingmale andfemalejurors.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
Directions: Read the following text and decide whether each of the statements is true or false.

Choose T if the statement is true or F if the statement is not true. Mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET 1. (10 points) Copying Birds May Save Aircraft Fuel Both Boeing and Airbus have trumpeted the efficiency of their newest aircraft, the 787 and A350 respectively. Their clever designs and lightweight composites certainly make a difference. But a group of researchers at Stanford University, led by Ilan Kroo, has suggested that airlines could take a more naturalistic approach to cutting jet-fuel use and it would not require them to buy new aircraft. The answer, says Dr. Kroo, lies with birds. Since 1914, scientists have known that birds flying in formation - a V-shape - expend less energy. The air flowing over a bird's wings curls upwards behind the wingtips, a phenomenon known as upwash. Other birds flying in the upwash experience reduced drag, and spend less energy propelling themselves. Peter Lissaman, an aeronautics expert who was formerly at Caltech and the University of Southern California, has suggested that a formation of 25 birds might enjoy a range increase of 71%. When applied to aircraft, the principles are not substantially different. Dr. Kroo and his team modeled what would happen if three passenger jets departing from Los Angeles, San Francisco and Las Vegas were to assemble over Utah, assume an inverted V-formation, occasionally change found that the aircraft consumed as much as 15% less fuel (coupled with a reduction in carbon-dioxide output). Nitrogen-oxide emissions during the cruising portions of the flight fell by around a quarter. There are, of course, knots to be worked out. One consideration is safety, or at least the perception of it. Would passengers feel comfortable travelling in companion? Dr. Kroo points out that the aircraft could be separated by several nautical miles, and would not be in the intimate groupings favoured by display teams like the Red Arrows. A passenger peering out of the window might not even see the other planes. Whether the separation distances involved would satisfy air-traffic-control regulations is another matter, although a working group at the International Civil Aviation Organisation has included the possibility of formation flying in a blueprint for new operational guidelines. It remains to be seen how weather conditions affect the air flows that make formation flight more efficient. In zones of increased turbulence, the planes’ wakes will decay more quickly and the effect will diminish. Dr. Kroo says this is one of the areas his team will investigate further. It might also be hard for airlines to co-ordinate the departure times and destinations of passenger aircraft in a way that would allow them to gain from formation flight. Cargo aircraft, in contrast, might be easier to reschedule, as might routine military flights. As it happens, America's armed forces are on the case already. Earlier this year the country's aircraft flew in formation when they were low on fuel during the Second World War, but Dr. Lissaman says they are unsubstantiated. “My father was an RAF pilot and my cousin the skipper of a Lancaster lost over Berlin," he adds. So he should know.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【试题考点】时间状语从句引导词辨析。
【解题思路】空格所在句指出：“在美国，随着较暖天气的到来，新发病例似乎逐渐减少（new cases seemed to fade as warmer weather arrived）。” 空格连接主句与从句，从句表示时间伴随与发展变化，“as”在此作连词引导时间状语从句，意为“随着，当……时”，符合文意，故选 [A]。
【错项排除】[B] if（如果）表假设条件；[C] unless（除非）表反向唯一条件；[D] until（直到……为止）常用于延续或否定结构，均不符合“天气转暖过程中病例逐渐减少”的自然伴随规律。

questions.stem: In the first paragraph, Damien Hirst's sale was referred to as "a last victory" because ______.

options.text: the art market had witnessed a succession of victories
the auctioneer finally got the two pieces at the highest bids
Beautiful Inside My Head Forever won over all masterpieces
it was successfully made just before the world financial crisis

questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。第一段提到达米恩·赫斯特的高价拍卖会于2008年9月15日举行，就在同一天雷曼兄弟宣布破产引爆全球金融海啸，因此这场拍卖会成为了金融危机前夕艺术市场的最后一次辉煌胜利（it was successfully made just before the world financial crisis）。

questions.stem: By saying "spending of any sort became deeply unfashionable" (Line 1-2, Para. 3), the author suggests that ______.

options.text: collectors were no longer actively involved in art-market auctions
people stopped every kind of spending and stayed away from galleries
art collection as a fashion had lost its appeal to a great extent
works of art in general had gone out of fashion so they were not worth buying

questions.explanation: 【考点】句意理解题。第三段紧随其后解释道‘In the art world that meant collectors stayed away from galleries and salerooms’，表明在大萧条阴云下，艺术收藏家们不再热衷出入画廊与拍卖行竞价买画（collectors were no longer actively involved in art-market auctions）。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: Sales of contemporary art fell dramatically from 2007 to 2008.
The art market surpassed many other industries in momentum.
The art market generally went downward in various ways.
Some art dealers were awaiting better chances to come.

questions.explanation: 【考点】是非判断题。文章第二段指出，艺术市场的暴跌速度与衰退幅度不仅没有超过其他实体工业，反而随着金融信贷紧缩同步陷入重创，甚至比其他行业的下跌更为剧烈，故 [B] 说法与原文事实相悖。

questions.stem: The three Ds mentioned in the last paragraph are ______.
questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。最后一段提到艺术圈著名的‘3D定律’——死亡（death）、债务（debt）和离婚（divorce），指出唯有这三种不可抗力的悲剧事件发生时，藏家才被迫将顶级艺术品推向市场变现，是促进艺术品流通的极端驱动因素（factors promoting artwork circulation）。

questions.stem: The most appropriate title for this text could be ______.
questions.explanation: 【考点】主旨大意题。全文围绕2008年华尔街金融危机重创全球当代艺术品市场、导致交易额断崖式下跌与买家离场展开论述，核心主题即艺术市场的全面衰退，故 Art Market in Decline 最契合主旨。

questions.stem: What is most wives' main expectation of their husbands?
questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。第四段明确指出，绝大多数妻子对婚姻最核心的诉求并非分担家务或金钱支持，而是希望丈夫首先能够成为一个耐心的交谈倾听伴侣（conversational partners / talking to them）。

questions.stem: Judging from the context, the phrase "wreaking havoc" (Line 3, Para. 2) most probably means ______.
questions.explanation: 【考点】词义猜测题。第二段指出两性之间截然相反的沟通模式正在严重侵蚀破坏许多原本完好的美满家庭，wreak havoc 属于固定习语，意为‘造成毁灭性破坏/带来严重损害’（causing damage）。

questions.stem: All of the following are true EXCEPT ______.

options.text: men tend to talk more in public than women
nearly 50 percent of recent divorces are caused by failed conversation
women attach much importance to communication between couples
a female tends to be more talkative at home than her spouse

questions.explanation: 【考点】是非判断题。第一段提到美国的离婚率接近50%，但在分析原因时指出缺乏沟通是主要导火索之一，并未武断断言‘50%的离婚全部是由沟通失败直接造成的’，[B] 夸大了统计关联度，故为错误选项。

questions.stem: Which of the following can best summarize the main idea of this text?

options.text: The moral decaying deserves more research by sociologists.
Marriage break-up stems from sex inequalities.
Husband and wife have different expectations from their marriage.
Conversational patterns between man and wife are different.

questions.explanation: 【考点】主旨大意题。全文从社会语言学角度深入剖析男女两性在公共场合与私人家庭中沟通谈话模式的本质差异，并揭示其对婚姻关系的深远影响，故 Conversational patterns between man and wife are different 最切中要害。

questions.stem: In the following part immediately after this text, the author will most probably focus on ______.

options.text: a vivid account of the new book Divorce Talk
a detailed description of the stereotypical cartoon
other possible reasons for a high divorce rate in the U.S.
a brief introduction to the political scientist Andrew Hacker

questions.explanation: 【考点】后续篇章推断题。文章末尾引出了社会学家针对婚姻对话出版的重磅新作《离婚对话》（Divorce Talk），按照行文承接规律，紧随其后的段落最有可能围绕该书的核心实证案例与深度洞察展开详细介绍（a vivid account of the new book Divorce Talk）。

questions.stem: According to Dr. Curtis, habits like hand washing with soap ______.
questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。第一段引述柯蒂斯博士的公共卫生研究指出，肥皂洗手等良好卫生习惯能够大幅降低传染病致死率，但全球仍有大量人群未养成这一反射性动作，因此必须进一步大力普及与培养（should be further cultivated）。

questions.stem: Bottled water, chewing gum and skin moisturizers are mentioned in Paragraph 5 so as to ______.

options.text: reveal their impact on people's habits
show the urgent need of daily necessities
indicate their effect on people's buying power
manifest the significant role of good habits

questions.explanation: 【考点】例证目的题。第五段列举瓶装水、口香糖与护肤霜，旨在作为商业广告营销成功塑造大众原本不存在的全新消费反射与日常习惯的典型案例（reveal their impact on people's habits）。

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT belong to products that help create people's habits?
questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节/常识题。文中提到的汰渍（Tide）、佳洁士（Crest）和高露洁（Colgate）均为具体的消费品商标产品，而联合利华（Unilever）是制造巨头跨国公司名称，非单一商品名称，故 [D] 符合题意。

questions.stem: From the text we know that some of consumers' habits are developed due to ______.
questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。通篇分析阐明，消费者的诸多日常习惯并非完全自主自发形成，而是跨国商业巨头通过铺天盖地的广告营销心理学战术精心设计与推广塑造出来的（commercial promotions）。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the influence of advertisement on people's habits is ______.
questions.explanation: 【考点】观点态度题。在最后一段中，作者尖锐指出当习惯塑造战术被不良企业用来推销可疑劣质护肤品或垃圾不健康食品时引发了巨大的社会伦理争议，对其滥用商业心理学操纵人性的做法持鲜明的否定批判态度（negative）。

questions.stem: From the principles of the US jury system, we learn that ______.

options.text: both literate and illiterate people can serve on juries
defendants are immune from trial by their peers
no age limit should be imposed for jury service
judgment should consider the opinion of the public

questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。第一段指出美国陪审团制度的宪政立法初衷，在于通过普通公民的参与审判，确保法庭判决能够真实反映市民社会与公众的朴素正义观念（judgment should consider the opinion of the public）。

questions.stem: The practice of selecting so-called elite jurors prior to 1968 showed ______.

options.text: the prevalent discrimination against certain races
the conflicting ideals in jury selection procedures
the arrogance common among the Supreme Court judges

questions.explanation: 【考点】推理判断题。第二段指出1968年以前所谓‘蓝带精英陪审员’制度在实践中造成了理想与现实的尖锐割裂：一方面宣称代表全社会，另一方面又以教育素质为由系统性排斥底层，暴露了遴选机制内部理念的严重冲突（the conflicting ideals in jury selection procedures）。

questions.stem: Even in the 1960s, women were seldom on the jury list in some states because ______.

options.text: they were automatically banned by state laws
they fell far short of the required qualifications
they were supposed to perform domestic duties
they tended to evade public engagement

questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。第三段明确提到，直到20世纪60年代部分州仍将女性排除在陪审团常备名单之外，其传统法理依据在于当时社会普遍认为女性的首要天职是操持家务与相夫教子（they were supposed to perform domestic duties）。

questions.stem: After the Jury Selection and Service Act was passed, ______.

options.text: sex discrimination in jury selection was unconstitutional and had to be abolished
educational requirements became less rigid in the selection of federal jurors
jurors at the state level ought to be representative of the entire community
states ought to conform to the federal court in reforming the jury system

questions.explanation: 【考点】事实细节题。第四段指出1968年《联邦陪审员遴选与服务法》彻底废除了陈旧严苛的文化考试与主观品德测试，使得联邦陪审员遴选的教育背景门槛大幅降低并更加平民化（educational requirements became less rigid in the selection of federal jurors）。

questions.stem: In discussing the US jury system, the text centers on ______.
questions.explanation: 【考点】主旨大意题。纵观全文，文章按照历史时间轴梳理了美国陪审团制度从早期的精英垄断、排斥妇女少数族裔的传统，逐步走向多元包容、平权立法的演进历程，其主线正是该制度的历史传统与改革发展，故 its tradition and development 最切题。

questions.stem: Findings of the Stanford University researchers will promote the sales of new Boeing and Airbus aircraft.

options.text: TRUE - The statement is true according to the passage.
FALSE - The statement is false according to the passage.

questions.explanation: 【考点】正误判断题。第一段末尾明确指出斯坦福大学的研究提出了一种更自然的节油方法，‘it would not require them to buy new aircraft’（无需航空公司采购新飞机），因此该项研究并不会促进波音和空客新飞机的销售，陈述与原文相悖，故为 FALSE。

questions.stem: The upwash experience may save propelling energy as well as reducing resistance.

options.text: TRUE - The statement is true according to the passage.
FALSE - The statement is false according to the passage.

questions.explanation: 【考点】正误判断题。第二段指出鸟类在上升气流（upwash）中飞行‘experience reduced drag, and spend less energy propelling themselves’（阻力减少，推动自身飞行的能量消耗降低），即同时减少了阻力并节省了推进动力，陈述与原文完全一致，故为 TRUE。

questions.stem: Formation flight is more comfortable because passengers can not see the other planes.

options.text: TRUE - The statement is true according to the passage.
FALSE - The statement is false according to the passage.

questions.explanation: 【考点】正误判断题。第四段指出飞机间距数海里、乘客甚至看不到其他飞机，是为了消除乘客对近距离伴飞的安全顾虑与心理不适（perception of safety），而非指飞行本身更舒适（more comfortable），曲解文意，故为 FALSE。

questions.stem: The role that weather plays in formation flight has not yet been clearly defined.

options.text: TRUE - The statement is true according to the passage.
FALSE - The statement is false according to the passage.

questions.explanation: 【考点】正误判断题。第五段首句明确提到‘It remains to be seen how weather conditions affect the air flows...’（天气状况如何影响气流仍有待观察和深入研究），表明气象条件在编队飞行中的作用尚未完全查明，故为 TRUE。

questions.stem: It has been documented that during World War II, America's armed forces once tried formation flight to save fuel.

options.text: TRUE - The statement is true according to the passage.
FALSE - The statement is false according to the passage.

questions.explanation: 【考点】正误判断题。最后一段提到二战期间美军战机低油量编队飞行的传闻时，航空专家利萨曼博士明确指出‘they are unsubstantiated’（这些传闻未经证实/缺乏事实依据），与题目‘It has been documented’（已有文献确凿记录）矛盾，故为 FALSE。
